## Highlights

This release closes six gaps where unsaved edits in **coyotenote-web** could be lost or hidden, and makes both apps notice outside edits that keep a note's size and time.

## coyotenote-web (experimental)

### Your edits are safer

- A dialog now stays open until its action finishes. Edits typed while a note was moving to the trash could be dropped when the move completed; that can no longer happen. **Undo** and restoring from the trash save what you typed while they waited.
- Undoing back to the last saved text while a save was still on its way no longer reads as "All changes saved". The undo stays recoverable as a browser draft until the save is confirmed.
- Notes with named HTML entities such as `&copy;` or `&nbsp;` open in Markdown view, because **Write** would have saved them as literal text. `&amp;`, `&lt;`, `&gt;` and `&quot;` still open in Write.
- A duplicated tab, or a window opened from one, now gets its own draft identity. Discarding a draft in one tab never deletes another open tab's only stored copy.
- When a note with an unsaved draft is renamed or deleted outside the app, a banner now says so. **Review drafts** lets you save each such draft as a note, download it or discard it.

## Both apps

- A note changed by another program is read again even when the change keeps the file's size and modification time. On Linux, macOS, FreeBSD and NetBSD the vault also checks the file's inode and change time. On every platform it reads again any file that changed within two seconds of being read.

## Downloads

One archive for **Linux amd64** holds `coyotenote`, `coyotenote-web`, the README, the license and third-party notices. Check it against `SHA256SUMS`. `govulncheck` and `npm audit` report no known vulnerabilities.
